feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: With the midterms fast approaching, campaign season begins
entry.summary: Labor Day marks the unofficial kickoff of the general election season as Republicans work to maintain control of the House and the Senate amid President Trump's unpopular second term.

entry.title: What to expect as midterm campaign season kicks off
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Charlie Cook, founder of the nonpartisan Cook Political Report, about the outlook for Democrats and Republicans as midterm campaign season kicks off.

entry.title: Public backlash against data centers is rising. Politicians are playing catchup
entry.summary: Public sentiment against data centers is running high this election season, leaving politicians of all stripes scrambling to respond. We look at how this is playing out in Pennsylvania.

entry.title: Politics chat: First-ever Republican midterm convention or Trump rally?
entry.summary: A first-ever Republican midterm convention is taking place this week in Dallas, but are candidates interested in attending? Plus, Michigan's Democratic senate candidate apologizes to Jewish voters.

entry.title: Witkoff and Kushner call Kyiv talks 'substantive' after Moscow Putin meeting
entry.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held meetings in Kyiv with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy on Sunday, a day after lengthy conversations with Russian President Putin in Moscow.

entry.title: Trump administration to dig at triumphal arch site despite no final federal approvals
entry.summary: The Trump administration says it will break ground on a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., without final federal approval and despite an ongoing lawsuit.

entry.title: Week in Politics: Trump's face on the coin; reshaping the capital; the midterms
entry.summary: President Trump is the first living president to have his face on a coin. He's also reshaping Washington in his image, and working to influence midterm elections.

entry.title: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are trying to cash in for midterms
entry.summary: Democrats and Republicans have found common ground in this campaign season. Both parties have poured millions into ads attacking data centers as the public continues to protest the AI facilities.

entry.title: Flock cameras draw opposition from across the political spectrum
entry.summary: As political races heat up heading into the midterms, candidates from both parties are increasingly joining the fray to voice concerns over Flock surveillance cameras.

entry.title: 4 things investigators learned about the dysfunction at Trump's Labor Department
entry.summary: A report from Labor Department investigators found former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer violated her own department's policy prohibiting harassment. She resigned in April.
